column3: “Oracle” is rendered “burden,” and “on” “against”; NASB puts the last clause in parentheses and renders it “the eyes of men, especially of all the tribes of Israel, are toward the LORD.” The meaning is uncertain.
“For it is very wise” is rendered “though they are very wise.”
“Strike in the sea her wealth” is rendered “cast her wealth into the sea.”
“Be in anguish” is rendered “writhe in great pain,” “object of confidence” “expectation,” and “ashamed” “confounded”; “remain” is rendered “be inhabited.”
“A mixed population” is rendered “a mongrel race.”
“Its” is rendered “their”; “left” is rendered “a remnant,” and “chief” “clan.”
“A guard” is rendered “because of an army”; NASB reads a different vowel pattern. The meaning is uncertain.
“Victorious” is rendered “endowed with salvation,” and “poor” “Humble”; “a male donkey, a young one of female donkeys” is rendered “a colt, the foal of a donkey.”
“Chariotry” is rendered “the chariot,” and “the river” “the River.”
“Your covenant” is rendered “My covenant with you,” and “I will set free” “I have set … free.”
“Prisoners of the hope” is rendered “prisoners who have the hope”; NASB supplies “that.”
“I will fill Ephraim” is rendered “I will fill the bow with Ephraim”; “on” is rendered “against.”
“Give a blast on the ram’s horn” is rendered “blow the trumpet,” and “go” “march.”
“Subdue stones of a sling” is rendered “trample on the sling stones”; NASB supplies “as with” and “Drenched,” and renders “bowl” as “sacrificial basin.”
“Display themselves” is rendered “Sparkling”; NASB supplies “they are.”
“Its goodness … its beauty” is rendered “what comeliness and beauty will be theirs”; “young women” is rendered “virgins,” and “cause to thrive” “make … flourish.”
